title: Bertie's Moon Race
markdown:
Bertie the bunny loved his special stones. He put them in order in his cozy home. Outside, Waffle the wombat munched a yummy carrot. The sun, a big orange ball, was getting sleepy. It painted the sky soft peachy colors.

Suddenly, Bertie hopped out of his home. His fluffy ears twitched with worry. He was tidying his books and found one hidden away. It was called "The Whispering Woods." On the back, a little red stamp winked.

"Oh dear, oh me, oh my!" Bertie said. His whiskers trembled a little. He felt worried. "This book is very, very, very late!"

Waffle stopped munching. His nose wrinkled. "Late?" he rumbled, his voice like soft stones rolling.

"Yes!" Bertie said, hopping closer. He held the book carefully. "The book wagon only comes once a week. And it leaves when the moon is bright and high in the sky! Look!" He pointed a small paw up. A sliver of moon, like a shy smile, was peeking out. "The moon will be big and round very soon! If the book is late, the book lady, Mrs. Winkle, will be sad."

Bertie's ears drooped a little. He didn't want Mrs. Winkle to be sad. This is a tricky spot, he thought. His nose wiggled with worry.

Waffle was kind. He finished his carrot. He patted Bertie's paw. "Don't worry, Bertie," he said. His voice was warm and steady. "We can take it back. We can be really, really fast!"

Bertie's eyes lit up. "A race!" he giggled. "A race against the moon! What an adventure!" He hopped up and down, feeling happy. "Come on, Waffle! Let's go!"

Bertie tucked "The Whispering Woods" safely under his arm. They set off. The path had sleepy flowers closing their petals. Soft grass tickled their feet. The moon climbed higher, shining a gentle, silvery light.

"We're going, we're going," Bertie puffed, taking big, excited hops.
"We're going, we're going," Waffle walked along next to him. His little tail gave a happy wag.

Soon, they came to a little stream. It gurgled and babbled happily. It was too wide for Bertie to hop. The water looked cool and splashy. Bertie's nose wiggled. "Oh," he wondered, his voice soft, "how will we get over?"

Waffle looked at the stream. He looked at Bertie's worried face. He let out a happy rumble. "Easy peasy, Bertie!" he said. "My waddle is perfect for streams!" He stepped into the water. It came up to his round tummy. He made himself a little bridge with his strong back. "Hop on, friend!" he called.

Bertie giggled. He held the book tight. He hopped onto Waffle's back. "Thank you, Waffle!" he squeaked. "You're a brilliant bridge!" Waffle waddled across steadily. Plish-plash went his feet. The stream seemed to giggle with them.

On the other side, the path was trickier. The moon was a big, happy circle, shining bright. They came to soft, glowy flowers. They looked like moonlight. When they tried to walk, the flowers wobbled and bounced them. "Moon-petals," Bertie whispered. The more they stepped, the more they bounced.

"Oh no!" Bertie exclaimed. The book almost tumbled. This is really tricky, he thought, his heart fluttering.

Waffle stopped. He let out a surprised chuckle. "They're tickly and wobbly!" he giggled.

Bertie looked around. He spotted a clearer patch of grass. It curved around the wobbly flowers. "Waffle!" he called. His voice was bright like a little bell. "Look! If we go this way, around the wobbly bits, we can sneak past!"

Waffle looked where Bertie pointed. "A clever path!" he said. They tiptoed carefully. The flowers swayed like friendly dancers. The moon watched with a bright smile, cheering them on.

Now, they saw the book wagon! It looked like a little wooden house on wheels. A warm lantern hung from its door. Mrs. Winkle, the book lady, was just closing up.

"Hurry, hurry!" Bertie urged, his bunny feet a blur.
"Almost there, almost there!" Waffle panted, his waddle turning into a quick pace.

They reached the wagon just as Mrs. Winkle was closing the door. The moon was at the very top of the sky, a perfect shining circle.

"We made it!" Bertie cheered, holding out the book with pride.
Mrs. Winkle smiled a wide, warm smile. "Well, hello there, Bertie and Waffle! Just in time! And what a wonderful adventure you must have had to bring 'The Whispering Woods' back so carefully." She took the book. "Thank you for being good readers."

Bertie and Waffle puffed out their chests. A warm glow spread through them. They hadn't been scared. They had helped each other. Bertie knew that even though he had worried a little, being brave with a good friend was the best adventure.

"We did it!" said Bertie, giving Waffle a happy nudge.
"We did it!" echoed Waffle, giving Bertie a gentle hug.

The moonbeams twinkled brighter. They turned to head home. The journey back felt even cozier. Bertie felt brave and happy. His friendship with Waffle shone as bright as the moon itself.
characters: Bertie the bunny, Waffle the wombat
